Subject: Change order request: add dedicated capacity + SOW alignment

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We talked internally and need to put a short change order in front of our procurement and legal teams. Two concrete asks:

1) Add 4 dedicated GPU nodes (heavy inference) for pilot month-to-month for 3 months, then convert to monthly reserved capacity.
2) Align Exhibit A (Implementation SOW) to remove the pilot-only carve and clarify acceptance criteria for throughput (p95 < 600ms).

Can you share a redline or proposed change order we can circulate? Procurement would like an estimate of the prorated fees for June and the contract language that controls conversion to reserved capacity. Marta (legal) will be reviewing technical clauses — CC'd.

Appreciate a quick turnaround, Evan

[Attachment: BRIGHT-CO_ChangeOrder-v1.docx (docx)]

Date: 2026-06-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Change order request: add dedicated capacity + SOW alignment

Evan —

Thanks — looping in Marissa (sales ops) for pricing/proration and Jonas (legal ops) for clause language. High-level approach:

- We'll propose a short Change Order that amends the Order Form to add a 3-month pilot of 4 GPUs as a separate line item (metered month-to-month), with explicit conversion language and a simple opt-in to convert to a 12-month reserved commitment at month 4.
- Exhibit A: supply a tracked redline that removes the pilot-only carve and adds the acceptance criteria you mentioned.
- Proration: Marissa will pull the June days-based proration and include a sample invoice line.

I attached a first-draft change order and a PDF with inline redlines to make legal review easier. Please flag the acceptance wording if you need stricter SLO language.

Best,
Laura

Evan / Laura —

Quick pricing/proration: assuming a June start on 6/20 and monthly billed list price for the 4-node pilot we estimate a prorated charge of $18,400 for the remainder of June (example calculation attached). If Brighthosp converts to a 12-month reserved commitment on 7/20 we will credit the prorated pilot fees against the first reserved invoice (see line 7 of the draft CO).

Notes:
- I left the conversion cap language intentionally permissive; if procurement wants a firm conversion window (e.g., conversion must occur by day 90) we can hardcode that.
- Adding a sentence that conversion pricing will be based on the rate card in effect at conversion is typical; happy to set a floor.

Attaching a spreadsheet and a short pricing note.

Hi Laura and team —

I reviewed the PDF redline. Two legal items we need clarified before procurement can approve:

1) Conversion mechanism: we need explicit language that states Brighthosp must provide written notice 30 days before the desired conversion month and that the conversion effective date will be the first day of the following billing month.
2) Data retention / log access during pilot: we require a 90-day audit trail for inference logs (an exhibit or footnote referencing Redwood's Console retention policy).

Also, Exhibit A acceptance criteria are OK but please tighten the p95 measurement window — we want a 30-day rolling window rather than a single test run.

If you can send an updated PDF with those three changes tracked, I can route to procurement for signature.

Thanks,
Marta (Brighthosp Legal)

Marta —

Thanks for the review. We've prepared an updated redline and tightened the language per your notes:

- Conversion clause now requires Brighthosp to provide written notice >=30 days prior to the conversion effective date; the effective date will be the first of the following calendar month.
- Exhibit A now references a 30-day rolling p95 window for throughput acceptance.
- Appendix 3 (Audit & Logs) added a 90-day retention requirement and a pointer to Redwood Console export capabilities; we've also included an ops contact for ad-hoc access requests.

I've attached the new PDF with tracked changes and a short plain-language summary of the edits to make legal handoff faster. If that looks good to you, Laura/Marissa can push the CO to DocuSign and we'll include the proration credit line.
